title: Till Reference on Scheduled Payments, Statements, Automatic Payment, Early Payoff and Overpayments — Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements
content:
# Till reference — payments and statements on a Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements agreement

Payments on an agreement of Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements fall due on the plan's frequency, each asking for the larger of the plan's minimum scheduled payment and the plan's share of the balance at opening. The balance at opening is read as the pre-tax merchandise price the agreement was opened at, and the share of it is carried to the cent. A payment is credited to an agreement only while it stands at opened, current, delinquent or on hold, and a statement is produced only for an agreement at one of those standings. A statement is produced on the plan's frequency and prints the next scheduled payment date; the plan that states only on request does so when the customer asks. Automatic payment is available on the plans that offer it, and while it is in force the holding fee is reduced by the plan's automatic payment discount. The agreement may be paid up early on every plan, and the plans that discount early payoff take their discount off the remaining balance. A payment that exceeds the balance is refunded as an overpayment rather than held on the agreement.

## Terms as the till applies them

| Matter | Term |
|---|---|
| When a payment falls due | on the plan's frequency |
| What a scheduled payment asks for | the larger of the plan's minimum scheduled payment and the plan's share of the balance at opening, carried to the cent |
| Which agreements a payment is credited to | those standing at opened, current, delinquent or on hold, read from the agreement record before the payment is credited |
| What a statement prints | the next scheduled payment date |
| When a statement is produced | on the plan's frequency; on the plan that states only on request, when the customer asks |
| Automatic payment | offered on the plans that say so; while in force, the holding fee is reduced by the plan's automatic payment discount |
| Early payoff | admitted on every plan; on the plans that discount it, the discount comes off the remaining balance |
| A payment larger than the balance | the excess is refunded as an overpayment, not held on the agreement |

## The scheduled payment on hypothetical figures

Take a plan whose minimum scheduled payment is, hypothetically, 50.00 and whose share of the balance at opening is 8.34 percent.

- An agreement opened at a merchandise price of 1500.00: the share is 125.10, which exceeds 50.00, so each scheduled payment asks for 125.10.
- An agreement opened at a merchandise price of 500.00: the share is 41.70, which is below 50.00, so each scheduled payment asks for 50.00.
- An agreement opened at a merchandise price of 1234.56: the share computes to 102.962304 and is carried to the cent as 102.96; each scheduled payment asks for 102.96.
